reference.source: GeneReviews and standard paediatric neurology references
clinicalPearls: A congenital overgrowth syndrome within the PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum (PROS).
Combines macrocephaly or megalencephaly with a midline facial capillary malformation and often reticulate or patchy capillary staining of the trunk and limbs.
Caused by somatic mosaic activating PIK3CA mutations.
Additional features include body asymmetry (hemihypertrophy), syndactyly or polydactyly, connective-tissue laxity, developmental delay and hypotonia.
Neuroimaging may show megalencephaly, ventriculomegaly, polymicrogyria and cerebellar tonsillar herniation.
There is a risk of progressive hydrocephalus and a Chiari-like malformation from ongoing brain overgrowth.
Cardiac arrhythmia has been reported and warrants baseline and periodic assessment.
Requires multidisciplinary neurodevelopmental, orthopaedic and neurosurgical follow-up.
reference.pathophysiology: Macrocephaly-capillary malformation is one of the PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum disorders, arising from postzygotic somatic mosaic activating mutations in PIK3CA that constitutively activate the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway and drive excessive cellular growth and proliferation in affected tissues. The mosaic distribution explains the segmental and asymmetric overgrowth, capillary malformations and brain overgrowth (megalencephaly) with cortical malformations such as polymicrogyria. Progressive brain and skull growth can secondarily cause ventriculomegaly, hydrocephalus and cerebellar tonsillar ectopia.
additionalDifferentials: Other PROS conditions such as CLOVES and Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
Sotos syndrome and other overgrowth syndromes
additionalInvestigations: Brain MRI for megalencephaly, polymicrogyria, ventriculomegaly and tonsillar herniation
Serial head circumference and growth measurements
Skeletal assessment for asymmetry and limb-length discrepancy
PIK3CA mutation testing on affected tissue, since blood may be mutation-negative in mosaic disease
redFlags: Signs of raised intracranial pressure or progressive hydrocephalus
Significant or progressive limb-length discrepancy and asymmetry
reference.prognosis: The condition is associated with variable developmental delay and neurological complications; prognosis depends on the severity of the brain malformation and overgrowth, and lifelong multidisciplinary surveillance is required.
pitfalls: Testing blood rather than affected tissue for the mosaic PIK3CA mutation and being falsely reassured by a negative result.
Attributing macrocephaly to a benign familial cause and missing megalencephaly.
Overlooking an evolving Chiari-like malformation or hydrocephalus.
Failing to arrange multidisciplinary developmental support.
